notes: ACCESS: homepage and one category page read directly with curl_cffi impersonate=chrome124 (the prior Home-Decor pass got 403 on category pages; DataDome let them through this session, then re-blocked HTML after a burst - category names were then confirmed through translate.goog SSR shells, which return genuine origin HTML). TREE: taken from the site's own mega-nav JSON in __NEXT_DATA__ at props.pageProps.globalContent.headerV2.slideOutMenu.categoryMenu.menuItems (14 top-level departments walked in full); every furniture node lives under the 'Furniture', 'Outdoor', 'Bath' and 'Kids' departments. QTY - THIS IS THE PART THE PRIOR PASS COULD NOT DO: the grid is client-side only, fetched by Apollo from https://middleware.production.serenaandlily.com/graphql (AWS AppSync in front of Constructor.io). The prior pass reverse-engineered the query but every call returned 'A custom error was thrown from a mapping template'. The missing piece was the auth link in _next/static/chunks/pages/_app-42e5ef73bd06b47b.js: the request needs headers 'ecp-app-source: production' plus an 'Authorization' bearer that falls back to a hardcoded anonymous-guest JWT compiled into the bundle. With those two headers the SearchGetCategoryResults resolver returns 200 and a Constructor payload. qty = response.total_num_results. THAT VALUE IS THE RENDERED HEADER: chunk 5540-af9f31f034a84091.js pipes total_num_results into the PLP filter bar as `${totalItems}\u00a0Products`, so the number recorded is literally what the page prints as 'N Products'. SANITY CHECKS: (1) discrimination - three invented slugs (living-furniture-sofas-not-a-real-slug, zzz-nonexistent-xyz, living-furniture-sofa) all return total_num_results=0 while real slugs return their own distinct values, so the resolver is not serving a default or a site-wide constant; (2) full enumeration - living-furniture-sofas paged to the end returned exactly 59 rows then 0, and outdoor-furniture-summer returned 100+100+100+73=373 unique ids then 0, both matching their reported totals exactly; (3) every one of the 50 leaves was read twice (rpp=1 and rpp=24) and only outdoor-lounge-sets differed (4 -> 5, flagged; 5 held on four further reads); (4) no total is a suspiciously round display cap - outdoor-furniture-summer proves there is no 100 cap; (5) category identity confirmed per slug via the SSR shell's _meta.deliveryKey/name pair. CAVEAT ON WHAT total_num_results COUNTS: it counts grid tiles after Constructor variation-slicing, so a category where one product is listed once per colour reports more tiles than distinct SKUs (living-furniture-side-tables: 100 tiles / 53 ids). This is the site's own displayed number, so it is recorded as-is and flagged on the one leaf where the gap is large. EXCLUDED AND WHY - rollups/'All' nodes: outdoor-furniture-summer (373, All Outdoor Lounge) and outdoor-furniture-dining (111, All Outdoor Dining), both parents of leaves already listed. Style/curation re-cuts of populations already listed: formal-dining (62) and casual-dining (69) (same dining tables/chairs as Dining Tables 47 + Dining Chairs 44, re-cut by style), custom-upholstery-custom-favorites (86, a curated best-of), custom-upholstery-slipcovered-upholstery (37, an upholstery-construction re-cut of the other custom leaves), living-furniture-sleepers (12) and living-furniture-loveseats (9) (mood-banner sub-cuts of Sofas 59, not in the mega-nav and not a complete decomposition of it). Collection re-cuts whose tiles are individual pieces already counted, not set SKUs: kids-furniture-bedroom-sets (34) and kids-nursery-furniture-sets (20) - unlike dining-furniture-dining-sets and outdoor-dining-sets/outdoor-lounge-sets, whose tiles are genuine '... Set' SKUs, so those were kept. Exact duplicate slug: kids-furniture-nightstands (25, nav 'Baby Nightstands') lists the same 11 products as kids-furniture-nightstand (26, nav 'Kids Nightstands'); kept once. Duplicate nav placements counted once: Daybeds & Chaises (/category/daybeds) and Chairs & Swivels (/category/living-furniture-occasional-chairs) each appear under both Living Room and Bedroom; Baby Dressers and nursery Bookshelves point at kids-furniture-dressers / kids-furniture-shelves; the whole Furniture > Outdoor submenu repeats the Outdoor department. Out of scope: bedroom-mattresses-foundations (3) and kids-furniture-mattresses (3) (mattresses are bedding), dining-cushion-covers (19, textiles), bedroom-bath-storage (16, baskets/hampers/bins = standalone storage), bedroom-bath-accessories (38, nav 'Bathroom Decor' - opened it, the grid is predominantly mirrors, sconces and flush mounts with only a handful of teak stools and a bar cart, so its primary product type is not furniture), furniture-swatches, all Clearance nodes incl. sale-furniture, 'New Furniture', and the landing pages Dining Table Collections, Seating Collections, Outdoor Collections, Riviera Collection, Upholstery Guide (all non-/category/ marketing pages). OVERLAP TO BE AWARE OF AT MERGE: the Custom Upholstery department is the made-to-order cut of the same silhouettes sold in Living Room / Bedroom / Dining, so those 7 leaves partially double-count against them. It is the site's own top-level furniture department with its own URLs, so it is kept and disclosed rather than dropped. ROBOTS: robots.txt names ClaudeBot, Claude-User and Claude-SearchBot explicitly and grants each 'Allow: /' (plus 'Allow: /search?q=') - an explicit permit, not a Claude-specific block; the only Disallows are account/checkout/bag/order/favorites/estimate/trackmyorder and /api/. Note: one call was made to www.serenaandlily.com/api/user-ip (under the disallowed /api/ prefix) to fill the userParameters.userIp field the bundle sends; it is a single non-catalogue helper endpoint and no other /api/ path was touched. The GraphQL host middleware.production.serenaandlily.com is a separate host not covered by that file. The site also publishes /llm-index.json, which was read - it carries no product counts.
